docs.title: Gennaro's Chicken
docs.text: Adapted from citalia.com.

docs.title: Chicken
docs.text:
• Chicken thighs, bone-in and skin-on: 4 pieces
  • Olive oil: 2 tbsp
  • Jalapeno: 1, whole
  • Garlic: 1 head, peeled
  • Fresh rosemary sprigs: 2–3

docs.title: Sauce
docs.text:
• Dry white wine: 100 ml
  • Chicken stock: 100 ml

docs.title: 1. Cold-Start Chicken
docs.text:
1. Season the chicken thighs generously with salt and black pepper.
  2. Put olive oil in dutch oven and add chicken, skin side down. Turn heat to medium high and cook until chicken releases and skin is golden brown.

docs.title: 2. Add Remaining Ingredients
docs.text:
1. Pour in the white wine and let it bubble for 1–2 minutes.
  2. Add the chicken stock.
  3. Add the garlic cloves, rosemary, and jalapeno.
  4. Cover the pan and cook gently for 30 minutes.

docs.title: 3. Serve
docs.text: 1. Transfer chicken to plates, spoon sauce and garlic over the top, and serve hot with bruschetta.

docs.title: Dough (~10 thin rounds)
docs.text:
• Warm water: 1 cup (240 g)
  • Instant yeast: 1.5 tsp (5 g)
  • Sugar: 1 tsp (4 g)
  • Bread: 3 cups (360 g)
  • Salt: 1.5 tsp (9 g)
  • Olive oil: 1 tbsp (15 g)

docs.title: Meat Topping
docs.text:
• Ground beef: 1.5 lb (~1 costco pack)
  • Onion: 1 medium (~150 g)
  • Garlic: 3 cloves (~12 g)
  • Red bell pepper: 1 small (~120 g)
  • Flat-leaf parsley: 1 cup packed (~40 g)
  • Tomato paste: 3 tbsp (50 g)
  • Olive oil: 2 tbsp (30 g)
  • Paprika: 2 tsp (4 g)
  • Aleppo pepper: 2 tsp (4 g)
  • Cumin: 1 tsp (2 g)
  • Salt: 15 g
  • Black pepper: 1 tsp (2 g)

docs.title: Garnish
docs.text:
• Lemon wedges
  • Onion–parsley–sumac

docs.title: 1. Make the Dough
docs.text:
1. Mix warm water, yeast, sugar. Rest 5 min.
  2. Add flour, salt, olive oil. Knead 8–10 min until smooth.
  3. Cover and rise 1 hour until doubled.
  4. Divide into 60 g balls (~10); rest 15 min.

docs.title: 2. Make the Topping
docs.text:
1. In the processor: onion chunks, garlic, bell pepper → pulse to a fine mince, not a puree.
  2. Add parsley → quick pulses to incorporate.
  3. Move veg mix to a bowl.
  4. Add ground beef, tomato paste, olive oil, paprika, Aleppo, cumin, salt, pepper.
  5. Mix thoroughly.

docs.title: 3. Shape the Bases
docs.text:
1. Preheat oven to 475°F. Place your sheet pan inside to preheat.
  2. Roll each dough ball very thin. You want almost tortilla-thin.

docs.title: 4. Assemble
docs.text:
1. Lay parchment on another sheet pan (not in the oven) and brush some oil on.
  2. Place rolled dough rounds on parchment. Spread a thin, even layer of topping, edge-to-edge.

docs.title: 5. Bake
docs.text:
1. Keep Sheet Pan A in the oven so it stays hot.
  2. Build each lahmacun on parchment on Sheet Pan B (counter).
  3. Slide parchment from B onto hot Pan A and bake ~8 minutes.
  4. While it bakes, assemble the next one on B.
  5. When A comes out, slide off the cooked one, slide the new parchment from B onto A, and return A to the oven.
  6. Repeat — A always stays hot in the oven; B is only for assembly.

docs.title: 6. Serve
docs.text:
• Squeeze lemon.
  • Add onion–parsley–sumac salad.
  • Roll and eat immediately.

docs.title: Rice & Patties
docs.text:
• White rice (dry): 3 cups
  • Beef patties: 4

docs.title: Gravy
docs.text:
• Unsalted butter: 3 Tbsp
  • All-purpose flour: 3 Tbsp
  • Beef stock: 2 cups
  • Soy sauce: 1 Tbsp
  • Worcestershire sauce: 1 tsp
  • Onion powder: ½ tsp
  • Garlic powder: ½ tsp
  • Black pepper: to taste

docs.title: To Serve
docs.text:
• Eggs: 4, crispy-fried
  • Optional: sliced scallions, furikake, togarashi

docs.title: 1. Cook the Rice
docs.text: 1. Start rice in the cooker so it finishes with everything else.

docs.title: 2. Make the Gravy
docs.text:
1. Melt butter in a saucepan over medium heat.
  2. Whisk in flour; cook 2–3 min until lightly golden and nutty.
  3. Slowly whisk in beef stock until smooth.
  4. Add soy, Worcestershire, onion powder, garlic powder, black pepper.
  5. Simmer until thick and glossy; adjust seasoning.

docs.title: 3. Cook the Patties
docs.text:
1. Grill hot and fast.
  2. Pull at 150°F.

docs.title: 4. Fry the Eggs
docs.text: 1. Fry eggs with crispy edges.

docs.title: 5. Assemble
docs.text:
1. In each bowl: rice → burger → ladle of gravy → fried egg.
  2. Garnish with scallions and furikake or togarashi.

docs.title: Mapo Tofu
docs.text: Adapted from Kenji's recipe on Serious Eats

docs.title: Ingredients
docs.text:
For the wok - 1/4 cup vegetable oil - 1/4 pound ground beef

Aromatics (combine in a small bowl) - 3 garlic cloves, grated on a microplane - 1 tablespoon fresh ginger, grated on a microplane

Braising sauce (combine in a small bowl or measuring cup) - 2 tablespoons fermented chili bean paste (doubanjiang) - 2 tablespoons amontillado sherry (sub for Shaoxing wine) - 1 tablespoon dark soy sauce - 1/4 cup chicken stock

Cornstarch slurry (combine in a small bowl) - 1 teaspoon cornstarch - 2 teaspoons cold water

Tofu - 1 1/2 pounds medium to firm silken tofu, cut into 1/2-inch cubes

To finish (combine in a small bowl — half the scallions only) - 1/4 cup roasted chili oil (already Sichuan-peppercorn infused — no need to make your own) - 1/4 cup finely sliced scallion greens, divided in half

Garnish (combine on a small plate) - Remaining scallion greens - Toasted ground Sichuan peppercorn (pre-made — no toasting/grinding needed)

docs.title: Instructions
docs.text:
1. Combine the cornstarch slurry ingredients in a small bowl, mixing with a fork until homogeneous. Bring a medium saucepan of water to a boil over high heat and add the tofu. Cook for 1 minute, then drain in a colander, being careful not to break up the tofu.
  2. Heat the vegetable oil in a wok over high heat until smoking. Add the beef and cook, stirring constantly, for 1 minute. Add the aromatics and cook until fragrant, about 15 seconds. Add the braising sauce and bring to a boil. Pour in the cornstarch slurry and cook for 30 seconds until thickened. Add the tofu and carefully fold in, being careful not to break it up too much. Stir in the chili oil and reserved half of scallions and simmer for 30 seconds longer. Transfer immediately to a serving bowl and top with the garnish. Serve immediately with white rice.

docs.title: Holy Basil Stir Fry (Pad Kra Pao)
docs.text: Adapted from the Hot Thai Kitchen Holy Basil Stir Fry recipe on hot-thai-kitchen.com.

docs.title: Stir-Fry
docs.text:
• Thai chilies: 10–30 g (5–10 chilies), or to taste
  • Garlic: 25 g (~5 cloves)
  • Fresno: 30 g (1 chili), chopped
  • Green beans: 60 g (½ cup), cut into short pieces
  • Onion: 50 g (½ small onion), diced
  • Ground chicken or pork: 300 g
  • Soy sauce: 15 g (1 Tbsp)
  • Fish sauce: 10 g (2 tsp)
  • Dark soy sauce: 7 g (1½ tsp)
  • Water: 30 g (2 Tbsp)
  • Sugar: 6 g (1½ tsp)
  • Basil: 40 g (1½ loosely packed cups)
  • Vegetable oil: ~15 g (1 Tbsp), as needed

docs.title: To Serve
docs.text:
• 2 fried eggs
  • Jasmine rice

docs.title: 1. Prepare Aromatics
docs.text:
1. Pound the Thai chilies into a fine paste.
  2. Add garlic and the mild red pepper; pound into a rough paste.

docs.title: 2. Make Sauce
docs.text: 1. In a small bowl, combine soy sauce, fish sauce, black soy sauce, water, and sugar; stir until sugar dissolves.

docs.title: 3. Stir-Fry
docs.text:
1. Heat a wok or large skillet over medium-high heat and add the vegetable oil.
  2. Sauté the garlic-chili paste until the garlic just begins to turn golden.
  3. Add the ground chicken; break it up and toss until evenly cooked.
  4. Pour in the sauce; continue tossing until the chicken is nearly done.
  5. Add onions and long beans (if using); toss until cooked through.
  6. Remove from heat and stir in the holy basil leaves just until wilted.

docs.title: 4. Fried Eggs
docs.text:
1. Heat about 1 cm of vegetable oil in a small pan over medium-high heat.
  2. Carefully crack in each egg and fry until the edges are bubbly and the yolk is cooked to your liking.

docs.title: 5. Serve
docs.text: 1. Serve the stir-fry over jasmine rice and top

docs.title: Prik Nam Pla (Thai Chili Fish Sauce)
Ingredients
docs.text:
• Thai chilies: 10–15 g (4–6 chilies), finely sliced or lightly crushed
  • Garlic: 6 g (1 small clove), finely sliced (optional)
  • Fish sauce: 30 g (2 Tbsp)
  • Lime juice: 15 g (1 Tbsp)
  • Sugar: 4 g (1 tsp)

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
1. In a small bowl, combine fish sauce, lime juice, and sugar. Stir until the sugar dissolves.
  2. Add the Thai chilies and garlic. Stir to combine. Let sit 5 minutes

docs.title: No-Knead Sourdough Bread
docs.text: Adapted from KingArthurBaking.com.

docs.title: Dough
docs.text:
• Ripe (fed) sourdough starter: 1 cup (227 g)
  • Lukewarm water: 1¾ cups (397 g)
  • Bread flour: 5 cups (600 g)
  • Table salt: 1 tablespoon (18 g)
  • Diastatic malt powder (optional): 2 teaspoons

docs.title: 1. Mix the Dough
docs.text:
1. Weigh or gently spoon flour into a measuring cup; level off.
  2. In a large bowl or bucket, combine all ingredients.
  3. Stir until the dough comes together into a rough, sticky mass; this should take about 30–60 seconds by hand or with a mixer on low speed.

docs.title: 2. Bulk Fermentation
docs.text:
1. Cover the dough and let it rise at room temperature for 1 hour.
  2. Using a wet hand, gently fold the dough over itself. Coil folds are good here.
  3. Cover and let rise for another 1 hour.
  4. Repeat the folds once more, then let the dough rise for a final 1 hour (total of 3 hours with two folds).
  5. Cover the dough and refrigerate for at least 8 hours and up to 48 hours.

docs.title: 3. Shape & Final Rise
docs.text:
1. Remove the dough from the refrigerator and allow it to warm at room temperature for 15 minutes.
  2. Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and gently shape into a round and plop into a banneton.
  3. Cover and let the dough rise 3 hours.

docs.title: 4. Bake
docs.text:
1. With a rack positioned in the middle, preheat the oven to 500°F one hour before baking.
  2. Just before baking, dust the loaf lightly with flour and score the top with one or more ½-inch-deep slashes.
  3. Cover the baker with its lid and place it in the oven. Reduce the oven temperature to 450°F and bake for 45 minutes.
  4. Remove the lid and continue baking for 10–15 minutes, until the crust is deep golden brown and a digital thermometer inserted into the center reads at least 210°F.

docs.title: 5. Serve
docs.text: 1. Remove the bread from the oven and transfer to a rack to cool completely before slicing.

docs.title: Sourdough Feeding Schedule
docs.text: Use a 1:1:1 ratio by weight (starter : flour : water).

docs.title: Example
docs.text: 20 g starter + 20 g flour + 20 g water = 60 g total starter

docs.title: Target amounts
docs.text:
• Starter needed for recipe 277 g
  • Starter to keep for next bake 40 g
  • Total starter to build 360 g

docs.title: Routine (minimal waste)
docs.text: 40 g → 120 g → 360 g → (use 277 g, save 40 g) → repeat

docs.title: Build example
docs.text:
1. Start with 40 g starter
  2. Feed with 40 g flour + 40 g water → 120 g total
  3. Feed again with 120 g flour + 120 g water → 360 g total

docs.title: After baking
docs.text:
• Remove 40 g starter
  • Transfer to a clean jar
  • Feed at 1:1:1
  • Let sit at room temperature for ~1 hour
  • Refrigerate

docs.title: Next bake
docs.text:
• Remove starter from fridge
  • Let it double and just begin to fall
  • Feed once to reach 360 g
  • Use 277 g in the recipe
  • Keep 40 g to restart the cycle

docs.title: Thai Red Curry
docs.text: Serves 2.

docs.title: Ingredients
docs.text:
• Coconut milk: 1 can (13.5 oz / 400 mL), unshaken
  • Red curry paste: 2–3 Tbsp, to taste
  • Chicken thighs, sliced, or silken tofu, in large pieces: 8–10 oz
  • Bell pepper: 1, sliced
  • Cherry tomatoes: 1 cup, whole
  • Fish sauce: 1–2 tsp, to taste
  • Palm sugar or brown sugar: 1–2 tsp
  • Thai basil: a handful, torn
  • Kaffir lime leaves (optional): 2–3, torn
  • Jasmine rice, for serving

docs.title: 1. Prep
docs.text:
1. Slice the chicken, or spoon the silken tofu out of its container into large, rough pieces (soondubu-style — don't dice it, keep it in soft, spoon-sized chunks).
  2. Slice the bell pepper.

docs.title: 2. Bloom the Paste
docs.text:
1. Scoop the thick coconut cream from the top of the unshaken can into a wok or pan over medium heat (skip if the can hasn't separated; use a splash of the coconut milk instead).
  2. Add the curry paste and cook, stirring, until fragrant and the oil starts to separate, 2–3 minutes.

docs.title: 3. Cook
docs.text:
1. If using chicken, add it now and stir until coated and the outside is no longer pink.
  2. Pour in the remaining coconut milk and bring to a gentle simmer.
  3. Add the bell pepper.
  4. If using chicken, simmer until the chicken is cooked through and the bell pepper is tender-crisp, 8–10 minutes. If using tofu, gently slide the pieces in along with the bell pepper and simmer just until warmed through, 3–4 minutes — spoon broth over the top rather than stirring, so the pieces stay large and intact.
  5. Add the cherry tomatoes whole in the last 1–2 minutes and simmer just until they soften, not so long that they burst and turn the curry watery.

docs.title: 4. Season
docs.text: 1. Stir in fish sauce and sugar, then taste and adjust — go easy on the fish sauce at first, since the curry paste is already well-salted.

docs.title: 5. Finish
docs.text: 1. Remove from heat and stir in the Thai basil and kaffir lime leaves (if using) just until wilted.

docs.title: 6. Serve
docs.text: Serve hot over jasmine rice.

docs.title: Chicken (Velveting)
docs.text:
• Boneless skinless chicken thighs, sliced: 1 lb
  • Soy sauce: 10 g / 2 tsp
  • Shaoxing wine: 10 g / 2 tsp
  • Cornstarch: 15 g / 1½ Tbsp
  • Neutral oil: 5 g / 1 tsp

docs.title: Sauce (Mix Before Cooking)
docs.text:
• Chicken stock: 180 g / ¾ cup
  • Soy sauce: 15 g / 1 Tbsp
  • Oyster sauce: 18 g / 1 Tbsp
  • Shaoxing wine: 15 g / 1 Tbsp
  • Sugar: 4 g / 1 tsp
  • Sesame oil: 2 g / ½ tsp
  • Cornstarch: 6 g / 1½ tsp

docs.title: Aromatics & Finish
docs.text:
• Garlic, minced: 6 g / 2 cloves
  • Ginger, minced (optional): 6 g / 1 Tbsp
  • Neutral oil: 15 g / 1 Tbsp
  • Sliced almonds, toasted: 30 g / ¼ cup
  • Scallions (optional): as needed

docs.title: 1. Velvet the Chicken
docs.text:
1. Combine chicken, soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, cornstarch, and oil.
  2. Toss until evenly coated.
  3. Rest 15–20 minutes at room temperature.

docs.title: 2. Toast the Almonds
docs.text:
1. Toast almonds in a dry pan over medium heat, stirring frequently.
  2. Remove once lightly golden and fragrant; set aside.

docs.title: 3. Stir-Fry the Chicken
docs.text:
1. Heat a wok or large skillet over high heat.
  2. Add neutral oil.
  3. Add chicken in a single layer and sear undisturbed for ~45 seconds.
  4. Stir-fry until just cooked through.
  5. Remove chicken to a plate.

docs.title: 4. Build the Sauce
docs.text:
1. Reduce heat slightly.
  2. Add garlic (and ginger, if using) and stir for ~10 seconds until fragrant.
  3. Stir sauce mixture well and pour into the pan.
  4. Simmer 20–30 seconds until thickened and glossy.

docs.title: 5. Combine
docs.text:
1. Return chicken to the pan.
  2. Toss to coat evenly with sauce.
  3. Fold in toasted almonds.

docs.title: 6. Serve
docs.text:
1. Garnish with scallions if using.
  2. Serve immediately with steamed white rice.

docs.title: Arroz Rojo (Basmati)
docs.text: Adapted from the Arroz Rojo recipe in La Mesa Mexicana.

docs.title: Rice
docs.text:
• 1½ cups (285g) basmati rice
  • 1 tablespoon lard
  • 2 garlic cloves, peeled
  • 2 serranos

docs.title: Tomato Mixture
docs.text:
• 2 large roma (plum) tomatoes, roughly chopped
  • ½ small white onion, roughly chopped
  • 85g (3 oz / ½ small can) tomato paste
  • 10g Better Than Bouillon chicken base
  • 1½ teaspoons Diamond Crystal kosher salt
  • Water, as needed to reach 3 cups total blended liquid

docs.title: 1. Make the Tomato Mixture
docs.text:
1. Place the tomatoes, onion, tomato paste, BTB, and salt in a blender.
  2. Blend until smooth, adding enough water to reach 3 cups total liquid.

docs.title: 2. Toast the Rice
docs.text:
1. Heat the lard in a large saucepan over medium–low heat.
  2. Add the garlic cloves and cook, stirring, for 1–2 minutes until lightly browned.
  3. Remove the garlic with a slotted spoon and discard.
  4. Add the rice to the pan and stir for 8 minutes, or until lightly toasted.

docs.title: 3. Cook the Rice
docs.text:
1. Stir in the blended tomato mixture until combined.
  2. Cover and bring to a boil.
  3. Reduce heat to low and cook for 20 minutes.
  4. Score shallow slits along each serrano and nestle them into the rice for the last 10 minutes of cooking.

docs.title: 4. Rest and Serve
docs.text:
1. Remove from heat and rest, lid on, for 5 minutes.
  2. Fluff with a fork and serve. Leftovers keep in an airtight container in the fridge for 3 days.

docs.title: Arroz Rojo
docs.text: Adapted from the Arroz Rojo recipe in La Mesa Mexicana.

docs.title: Rice
docs.text:
• 1½ cups (285g) long-grain white rice
  • 1 tablespoon lard
  • 2 garlic cloves, peeled
  • 2 serranos

docs.title: Tomato Mixture
docs.text:
• 2 large roma (plum) tomatoes, roughly chopped
  • ½ small white onion, roughly chopped
  • 85g (3 oz / ½ small can) tomato paste
  • 10g Better Than Bouillon chicken base
  • 1 teaspoon Diamond Crystal kosher salt
  • Water, as needed to reach 3 cups total blended liquid

docs.title: 1. Make the Tomato Mixture
docs.text:
1. Place the tomatoes, onion, tomato paste, BTB, and salt in a blender.
  2. Blend until smooth, adding enough water to reach 3 cups total liquid.

docs.title: 2. Toast the Rice

1. Heat the lard in a large saucepan over medium–low heat.
  2. Add the garlic cloves and cook, stirring, for 1–2 minutes until lightly browned.
  3. Remove the garlic with a slotted spoon and discard.
  4. Add the dry rice to the pan and stir for 8 minutes, or until lightly toasted.

docs.title: 3. Cook the Rice

  3. Reduce heat to low and cook for 25 minutes.
  4. Score shallow slits along each serrano and nestle them into the rice for the last 10 minutes of cooking.

docs.title: Chickpeas & Base
docs.text:
• Garbanzo beans (canned, drained): 480 g / 2 cups (1–2 cans)
  • Onion, finely chopped: 200 g / ~1½ cups
  • Neutral oil (or ghee): 30 g / 2 Tbsp
  • Salt: 6 g / 1 tsp, plus more to taste
  • Water or stock: 240–360 g / 1–1½ cups
  • Reserved aquafaba (optional): 30–60 g / 2–4 Tbsp

docs.title: Aromatics (optional but recommended)
docs.text:
• Garlic, minced: 12 g / ~4 cloves
  • Ginger, minced: 10 g / ~1 Tbsp

docs.title: Spices
docs.text:
• Curry powder: 4–5 g / 1½–2 tsp
  • Ground cumin: 1–2 g / ½–1 tsp
  • Ground coriander (optional): 1 g / ½ tsp
  • Ground turmeric: 0.5 g / ¼ tsp
  • Chili powder: to taste
  • Garam masala: 2 g / ¾–1 tsp
  • Kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves): 1 g / ~1 tsp, crushed

docs.title: 1. Build the Onion Base
docs.text:
1. Heat oil in a pan over medium heat.
  2. Add onion and salt.
  3. Cook, stirring occasionally, until soft and lightly golden, 8–12 minutes.
  4. If using garlic and ginger, add and cook 30–60 seconds until fragrant.

docs.title: 2. Bloom the Spices
docs.text:
1. Lower heat slightly.
  2. Add curry powder, cumin, coriander, turmeric, and chili powder.
  3. Stir constantly for 30–45 seconds until fragrant, adding a splash of water if dry.

docs.title: 3. Add Chickpeas and Liquid
docs.text:
1. Add chickpeas and stir to coat with the spiced onion mixture.
  2. Add water or stock and optional aquafaba.
  3. Bring to a gentle simmer.

docs.title: 4. Simmer and Thicken
docs.text:
1. Simmer uncovered for 10–15 minutes.
  2. Mash some chickpeas against the side of the pan to thicken the sauce.
  3. Adjust salt as needed.

docs.title: 5. Finish
docs.text:
1. Turn off heat.
  2. Stir in garam masala.
  3. Crush kasuri methi between your palms and add.
  4. Cover and rest 2–3 minutes.

docs.title: 6. Serve
docs.text: Serve hot over rice.

docs.title: Shrimp
docs.text:
• Shrimp (21–30 count): 225 g / 8 oz, peeled & deveined
  • Cornstarch: 5 g / 1 tsp
  • Salt: 1 g / ¼ tsp
  • Neutral oil: 5 g / 1 tsp

docs.title: Aromatics & Vegetables
docs.text:
• Pixian doubanjiang: 15 g / 1 Tbsp
  • Garlic: 12 g / ~4 cloves, minced
  • Ginger: 10 g / ~1 Tbsp, minced
  • Scallions (white parts): 20 g / ~2, sliced
  • Red bell pepper: 100 g / ~1 cup, julienned

docs.title: Fish-Fragrant Sauce Base (mix fully before cooking)
docs.text:
• Sugar: 10 g / 2½ tsp
  • Chinkiang black vinegar: 15 g / 1 Tbsp
  • Light soy sauce: 10 g / 2 tsp
  • Cornstarch: 5 g / 1 tsp
  • Chicken stock or water: 60 g / ¼ cup

docs.title: 1. Prep Shrimp
docs.text:
1. Toss shrimp with salt, cornstarch, and oil.
  2. Set aside while heating the wok.

docs.title: 2. Sear Shrimp
docs.text:
1. Heat wok over medium-high until lightly smoking.
  2. Add 1 Tbsp oil.
  3. Add shrimp in a single layer.
  4. Cook 30–45 seconds per side until just opaque.
  5. Remove immediately and set aside.

docs.title: 3. Bloom the Doubanjiang
docs.text:
1. Lower heat to medium.
  2. Add 1 Tbsp oil.
  3. Add Pixian doubanjiang by itself.
  4. Stir 20–30 seconds until oil turns red and fragrant.
  5. Do not brown.

docs.title: 4. Aromatics
docs.text:
1. Add garlic, ginger, and scallion whites.
  2. Stir 10–15 seconds, just until fragrant.

docs.title: 5. Vegetables & Sauce
docs.text:
1. Add bell pepper and stir once.
  2. Re-stir the prepared sauce base and pour into the wok.
  3. Let bubble uncovered 20–30 seconds until glossy and thickened.

docs.title: 6. Finish Shrimp
docs.text:
1. Return shrimp to the wok.
  2. Toss 20–30 seconds until coated and cooked through.

docs.title: 7. Serve
docs.text:
1. Optional: finish with ½ tsp sesame oil and scallion greens.
  2. Serve immediately with rice.

docs.title: Green Chile Braised Chicken Thighs with Corn
Chicken
docs.text:
• 6 boneless, skinless chicken thighs (about 680g / 1.5 lb)
  • 1/2 tsp kosher salt
  • 1/4 tsp black pepper
  • 15 ml (1 tbsp) avocado or grapeseed oil

docs.title: Braise
docs.text:
• 120g (1/2 medium) white onion, diced
  • 2 garlic cloves, minced
  • 1/2 tsp ground cumin
  • 1/2 tsp dried Mexican oregano
  • About 225g (1/2 of a 16 oz jar) roasted green chiles, drained and chopped, liquid reserved
  • 240 ml (1 cup) low-sodium chicken stock
  • 1 bay leaf
  • 150g (about 1 cup) fire-roasted corn kernels

docs.title: Thickener
docs.text:
• 8g (1 tbsp) masa harina (Maseca)
  • 30 ml (2 tbsp) water

docs.title: To finish
docs.text:
• 15 ml (1 tbsp) fresh lime juice
  • 8g (2 tbsp) chopped cilantro
  • Cotija, crumbled, for serving (optional)

docs.title: 1. Sear the chicken
docs.text: Season chicken thighs with the salt and pepper. Heat oil in a Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high until shimmering. Sear thighs in batches, 3 minutes per side, until golden but not cooked through. Remove and set aside.

docs.title: 2. Build the aromatic base
docs.text: Lower heat to medium. Add onion to the pot, cooking 4-5 minutes until softened. Add garlic, cumin, and oregano, stirring 30 seconds until fragrant.

docs.title: 3. Add chiles and braise
docs.text: Stir in the chopped green chiles, reserved chile liquid, chicken stock, and bay leaf. Return chicken thighs to the pot, nestling them into the liquid. Bring to a simmer, then cover and reduce heat to low. Braise 25-30 minutes, until chicken is fork-tender.

docs.title: 4. Add the corn
docs.text: Stir in the corn kernels and simmer uncovered for 5 minutes.

docs.title: 5. Thicken the sauce
docs.text: Whisk masa harina with the water to form a smooth slurry. Stir into the pot and simmer uncovered 5-8 minutes, until the sauce thickens and coats the back of a spoon.

docs.title: 6. Adjust and finish
docs.text: Remove bay leaf. Stir in lime juice. Taste and adjust salt.

docs.title: 7. Serve
docs.text: Serve in shallow bowls topped with cilantro and cotija, with warm corn tortillas alongside.

docs.title: Rice
docs.text: • 300g / 1½ cups basmati rice

docs.title: Liquid
docs.text:
• 530ml / 2¼ cups water
  • 12g / 2 tsp Better Than Bouillon paste
  • 3 gelatin ice cubes

docs.title: Aromatics
docs.text:
• 1 medium yellow onion, halved and thinly sliced
  • 4 cloves garlic, minced
  • ½ tsp ground ginger

docs.title: Whole Spices
docs.text:
• 1½ tsp cumin seeds
  • 4 green cardamom pods, cracked
  • 4 whole cloves
  • 1 cinnamon stick (or ¼ tsp ground)

docs.title: Ground Spices & Finish
docs.text:
• ¼ tsp turmeric
  • ¼ tsp garam masala (finish only)
  • 1 tsp Diamond Crystal kosher salt, plus more to taste
  • 20–25 saffron threads
  • 2 tbsp ghee or butter

docs.title: 1. Soak the Rice
docs.text: Rinse the rice under cold water until it runs clear, then soak in cold water for 30 minutes. Drain well before using.

docs.title: 2. Fry the Onion
docs.text: Heat the ghee in a heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add the sliced onion with a pinch of salt and cook, stirring occasionally, for 10–12 minutes until deep golden and beginning to crisp at the edges. Remove about a third of the onion and set aside on a paper towel — this is your garnish.

docs.title: 3. Bloom the Whole Spices
docs.text: Reduce heat to medium. Add the cumin seeds, cardamom pods, cloves, and cinnamon directly to the onion remaining in the pot. Stir constantly for 60–90 seconds until the cumin is fragrant and starting to darken. Add the garlic and ground ginger and cook another 60 seconds.

docs.title: 4. Toast the Rice
docs.text: Add the drained rice to the pot and stir to coat every grain in the spiced fat. Add the turmeric and 1 tsp Diamond Crystal kosher salt. Toast for 2 minutes, stirring gently.

docs.title: 5. Cook
docs.text: Pull 2 tbsp of water into a small bowl, add the saffron threads, and steep for 10 minutes. Pour the remaining water into the pot along with the Better Than Bouillon paste and gelatin ice cubes and stir to dissolve. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to the lowest setting. Drizzle the saffron liquid over the top without stirring it in. Cover tightly with a lid (use foil under the lid if it's not snug) and cook for 12 minutes undisturbed.

docs.title: 6. Steam and Rest
docs.text: Turn off the heat and let the pot sit covered for 10 minutes. Do not lift the lid.

docs.title: 7. Serve
docs.text: Uncover, add the garam masala, and fluff gently with a fork. Taste and adjust salt. Plate and top with the reserved crispy onion.

docs.title: Malasadas
docs.text: Adapted from the Malasadas recipe on Hummingbird High.

docs.title: For the Malasada Dough
docs.text:
• 2 cups (255 g) bread flour, plus more for assembly
  • 1 teaspoon granulated sugar
  • 7g instant yeast
  • ½ teaspoon kosher salt
  • ¾ cup (170 g) whole milk, warmed to 120–130 °F
  • 1 large egg, at room temperature
  • 1 large egg yolk, at room temperature
  • 2 Tablespoons (28 g) unsalted butter, melted and cooled slightly

docs.title: For the Passion Fruit Pastry Cream
docs.text:
• 6 Tablespoons (≈75 g) granulated sugar — divided: ¼ cup (≈50 g) + 2 Tablespoons (≈25 g)
  • 1 cup (227 g) whole milk
  • 1 large egg
  • 2 Tablespoons (28 g) cornstarch
  • ¼ teaspoon kosher salt
  • 1 Tablespoon (14 g) unsalted butter
  • ¼ cup (57 g) passion fruit puree
  • ¼ teaspoon pure vanilla extract

docs.title: For Assembly / Frying
docs.text:
• Vegetable oil, for frying
  • ¾ cup (149 g) granulated sugar, for coating

docs.title: 1. Make the Dough & Pastry Cream (Day 1)
docs.text:
1. In a stand mixer fitted with a dough hook, combine the flour, 1 tsp sugar, yeast, and salt. Stir briefly to combine, then press a well in the center.
  2. In a separate liquid measuring cup, whisk together the warm milk, egg, egg yolk, and melted butter.
  3. Pour the wet ingredients into the flour well. Knead on medium-low for 10 minutes (using a rubber spatula or plastic bench scraper to scrape down the bowl). Dough will be sticky, like a thick batter.

  4. Cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate overnight.

  5. Meanwhile, make the pastry cream: In a medium saucepan, whisk the ¼ cup (≈50 g) sugar with the milk. Heat over medium-low, whisking until milk steams (2–3 min), then reduce heat to low.

  6. In a bowl, whisk together the egg, salt, cornstarch, and remaining 2 Tablespoons (≈25 g) sugar. Temper by slowly adding about ¼ cup of the hot milk mixture while whisking continuously.
  7. Pour the tempered egg mixture back into the saucepan with the rest of the hot milk mixture. Return to medium heat and cook, whisking constantly, until it "boils". Immediately remove from heat.
  8. Add the butter, passion fruit puree, and vanilla. Whisk until smooth.
  9. Strain the cream through a fine-mesh sieve into an airtight container. Press plastic wrap directly on its surface to prevent a skin from forming. Chill overnight in the refrigerator.

docs.title: 2. Shape, Proof & Fry (Day 2)
docs.text:
1. Line a half-sheet pan with parchment paper and lightly flour it. Remove dough from fridge, discard plastic wrap, dump onto a well-floured counter and roll into a rectangle about ½-inch thick.
  2. Use a 3-inch round cookie cutter to cut 6 circles; re-roll scraps if necessary. Place circles at least 3 inches apart on the sheet pan. Cover loosely with plastic wrap and let rise for 1 hour.
  3. Meanwhile, fill a heavy-bottomed pot (or deep-fryer) halfway with vegetable oil. Attach a deep-fry thermometer; heat oil to 365 °F. Line a wire rack with paper towels. Put the ¾ cup (149 g) sugar for coating in a shallow bowl. Transfer the chilled pastry cream to a pastry bag fitted with a long nozzle tip (e.g. Bismark tip).
  4. Working in small batches (2 donuts at a time recommended), carefully lift each circle with a floured bench scraper, and fry for about 2 minutes per side, until golden and puffy. Use a slotted spoon to transfer to the wire rack. Maintain oil temperature at 365 °F between batches.
  5. While still warm, roll each donut in the shallow bowl of sugar. Let donuts cool for about 15 minutes.
  6. Use a skewer or the pastry tip to poke a hole in the side of each donut. Pipe ~2 Tablespoons of pastry cream into each donut until full and slightly stretched.

docs.title: 3. Serve
docs.text:
• Serve warm or at room temperature.
  • Best eaten the day they’re made. For leftovers: cover under a cake dome or inverted bowl for up to 1 day. After that, transfer to an airtight container and refrigerate for up to 2 more days.

docs.title: Quinoa Bibimbap Meal Prep Bowls
docs.text: Adapted from a bibimbap bowl, reworked into weekly meal prep with quinoa in place of rice and Bibigo Korean BBQ marinade for the beef.

docs.title: Quinoa
docs.text:
• 340g (2 cups) white quinoa, rinsed
  • 15ml (1 tbsp) neutral oil, for toasting
  • 680ml (2¾ cups) chicken or beef stock
  • 1/2 tsp Diamond Crystal kosher salt

docs.title: Beef
docs.text:
• 680g (1.5 lb) thin-sliced beef (ribeye or sirloin style)
  • 240ml (1 cup) Bibigo Korean BBQ marinade
  • 15ml (1 tbsp) neutral oil, for searing

docs.title: Spinach Gomae
docs.text:
• 340g (12 oz) baby spinach
  • 15ml (1 tbsp) toasted sesame oil
  • 15ml (1 tbsp) Kikkoman soy sauce
  • 1 tsp toasted sesame seeds
  • 1 clove garlic, grated

docs.title: Bean Sprouts (Kongnamul)
docs.text:
• 340g (12 oz) fresh bean sprouts
  • 10ml (2 tsp) toasted sesame oil
  • 1/2 tsp Diamond Crystal kosher salt
  • 1 scallion, thinly sliced

docs.title: Carrot
docs.text:
• 3 large carrots, julienned (~300g)
  • 10ml (2 tsp) neutral oil
  • 1/4 tsp Diamond Crystal kosher salt

docs.title: Mushroom
docs.text:
• 227g (8 oz) shiitake mushrooms, stemmed and sliced
  • 15ml (1 tbsp) toasted sesame oil
  • 15ml (1 tbsp) Kikkoman soy sauce
  • 1/2 tsp sugar

docs.title: Gochujang Sauce
docs.text:
• 60g (3 tbsp) Chung Jung One gochujang
  • 15ml (1 tbsp) toasted sesame oil
  • 15ml (1 tbsp) Marukan rice vinegar
  • 1 tsp sugar
  • 1 clove garlic, grated

docs.title: Daily (not batched)
docs.text: • 1 egg per bowl, fried, crispy edges/runny yolk

docs.title: 1. Toast and Cook the Quinoa
docs.text: Heat the neutral oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the rinsed and dried quinoa and toast, stirring, for 2-3 minutes until fragrant and lightly golden. Add the stock and salt, bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer, cover, and cook 15 minutes until liquid is absorbed. Fluff and let cool before portioning.

docs.title: 2. Marinate and Sear the Beef
docs.text: Toss the thin-sliced beef with the Bibigo marinade and let sit at least 30 minutes (up to a few hours in the fridge). Heat oil in a pan or on a griddle over high heat. Sear the beef in batches, not crowding the pan, 1-2 minutes per side until charred at the edges. Set aside to cool before portioning.

docs.title: 3. Blanch the Spinach
docs.text: Bring a pot of water to a boil. Blanch spinach 30 seconds, then shock in cold water. Squeeze out as much liquid as possible. Toss with sesame oil, soy sauce, sesame seeds, and grated garlic.

docs.title: 4. Blanch the Bean Sprouts
docs.text: In the same pot, blanch bean sprouts 2 minutes until just tender. Drain and shock briefly in cold water. Toss with sesame oil, salt, and scallion.

docs.title: 5. Sauté the Carrot
docs.text: Heat neutral oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Add julienned carrot and salt, sauté 2-3 minutes until just softened but still with bite.

docs.title: 6. Sauté the Mushroom
docs.text: In the same pan, sauté shiitake in sesame oil until browned, about 4 minutes. Add soy sauce and sugar, toss to coat, cook 1 more minute.

docs.title: 7. Make the Gochujang Sauce
docs.text: Whisk together gochujang, sesame oil, rice vinegar, sugar, and grated garlic until smooth. Store in a squeeze bottle or jar.

docs.title: 8. Serve
docs.text: Portion quinoa, beef, and each namul into containers for the week. Each morning, fry an egg to your liking and add fresh on top along with a drizzle of gochujang sauce just before eating.

docs.title: Protein & Beans
docs.text:
• Boneless, skinless chicken thighs: ~600g / 4 thighs
  • Canned cannellini beans: 400g / 1 can, drained and rinsed

docs.title: Aromatics & Fat
docs.text:
• Yellow onion: 150g / 1 medium, diced
  • Garlic: 20g / 4 cloves, minced or smashed
  • Olive oil: 30g / 2 tbsp

docs.title: Liquid
docs.text:
• Dry white wine: 120g / ½ cup (or sub additional chicken stock)
  • Chicken stock: 360g / 1½ cups

docs.title: Herbs
docs.text:
• Fresh thyme: 6–8 sprigs
  • Fresh sage: 4 large leaves
  • Bay leaf: 1 (if you have it)

docs.title: Seasoning
docs.text:
• Diamond Crystal kosher salt: to taste
  • Black pepper: to taste

docs.title: 1. Season and Sear the Chicken
docs.text: Pat chicken thighs dry and season aggressively with salt and pepper on both sides. Heat oil in a Dutch oven or heavy oven-safe skillet over medium-high. Sear chicken thighs presentation-side down for 4–5 minutes until deeply golden. Flip and sear 2 minutes more. Remove and set aside — they won't be cooked through yet.

docs.title: 2. Build the Base
docs.text: Pour off all but 1 tbsp of fat. Reduce heat to medium, add onion with a pinch of salt, and cook 5–6 minutes until softened. Add garlic and cook 1 minute more. Add sage leaves whole — let them sizzle briefly in the oil to bloom.

docs.title: 3. Deglaze and Add Liquid
docs.text: Add white wine and scrape up any fond. Let reduce by half, about 2 minutes. Add stock, thyme sprigs, and bay leaf if using. Season the liquid — it should taste well-seasoned before the chicken goes back in.

docs.title: 4. Braise
docs.text: Return chicken thighs to the pot, nestled into the liquid. Bring to a bare simmer, cover, and cook over low heat for 25 minutes — or transfer to a 325°F / 165°C oven for more even heat.

docs.title: 5. Add Beans and Finish
docs.text: Add drained cannellini beans, stirring gently around the chicken. Taste and adjust salt. Simmer uncovered for 10–15 minutes until the liquid reduces to a light, brothlike sauce that coats the beans.

docs.title: 6. Serve
docs.text: Discard thyme stems, sage leaves, and bay leaf. Let rest 5 minutes. Serve in wide bowls — crusty bread alongside is ideal for the braising liquid.

docs.title: Aglio e Olio
docs.text: Serves 2.

docs.title: Ingredients
docs.text:
• Dried spaghetti: 8 oz (227 g)
  • Garlic: 4–6 cloves, thinly sliced
  • Extra virgin olive oil: ⅓ cup (80 mL)
  • Red pepper flakes: ½–1 tsp, to taste
  • Fresh parsley, chopped: ¼ cup
  • Salt: for pasta water, plus more to taste
  • Black pepper: to taste

docs.title: 1. Prep
docs.text:
1. Thinly slice the garlic.
  2. Chop the parsley.

docs.title: 2. Cook the Pasta
docs.text:
1. Bring a large pot of well-salted water to a boil.
  2. Cook the pasta until al dente.
  3. Reserve at least 1 cup of the pasta water, then drain the pasta.

docs.title: 3. Infuse the Oil
docs.text:
1. While the pasta cooks, warm the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-low heat.
  2. Add the garlic and red pepper flakes. Cook gently, stirring often, until the garlic is fragrant and just turning golden, 2–3 minutes — don't let it brown or burn, or it turns bitter.

docs.title: 4. Combine
docs.text:
1. Add the drained pasta to the skillet and toss to coat in the oil.
  2. Add a splash of the reserved pasta water and toss, adding more a little at a time, until the sauce clings lightly to the pasta.

docs.title: 5. Finish
docs.text:
1. Remove from heat and stir in the parsley.
  2. Taste and season with salt and black pepper as needed.

docs.title: 6. Serve
docs.text: Serve immediately.

docs.title: Carbonara
docs.text: Serves 2.

docs.title: Ingredients
docs.text:
• Dried spaghetti: 8 oz (227 g)
  • Guanciale, diced: 2.5 oz (70 g)
  • Large egg yolks: 2
  • Large egg: 1
  • Parmigiano Reggiano, finely grated: 1.5 oz (45 g), plus more for serving
  • Freshly cracked black pepper: to taste, plus more for serving
  • Salt: for pasta water

docs.title: 1. Prep
docs.text:
1. Dice the guanciale into small (¼-inch) pieces.
  2. Finely grate the Parmigiano Reggiano.
  3. In a bowl, whisk together the egg yolks, whole egg, grated cheese, and a generous amount of black pepper until well combined. Set aside.

docs.title: 2. Render the Guanciale
docs.text:
1. Add the guanciale to a cold skillet and set over medium-low heat.
  2. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the fat has rendered and the guanciale is crisp and golden, about 8–10 minutes.
  3. Remove from heat; leave the guanciale and rendered fat in the pan.

docs.title: 3. Cook the Pasta
docs.text:
1. Bring a large pot of well-salted water to a boil.
  2. Cook the pasta until just shy of al dente (about 1 minute less than package directions).
  3. Reserve at least 1 cup of the pasta water, then drain the pasta.

docs.title: 4. Combine
docs.text:
1. Add the drained pasta to the skillet with the guanciale and toss to coat in the rendered fat.
  2. Remove the skillet from heat and let cool for about 30 seconds, so the eggs don't scramble.
  3. Add a splash of the reserved pasta water to the egg mixture to temper it, then pour over the pasta, tossing constantly.
  4. Continue tossing, adding reserved pasta water a little at a time, until the sauce is smooth, glossy, and coats the pasta.

docs.title: 5. Serve
docs.text: Divide between two bowls and top with additional grated Parmigiano Reggiano and black pepper. Serve immediately.

docs.title: Tomato Sauce
docs.text: Adapted from Marcella Hazan's tomato sauce, from Essentials of Classic Italian Cooking.

docs.title: Ingredients
docs.text:
• Canned whole peeled San Marzano tomatoes: 28 oz (794 g), with their juice
  • Butter: 5 tablespoons (70 g)
  • Yellow onion: 1 medium, peeled and halved
  • Salt: to taste

docs.title: 1. Cook
docs.text:
1. Add the tomatoes and their juice to a saucepan along with the butter and onion halves. Hold off on adding salt for now — the butter is already salted.
  2. Set over medium heat and bring to a simmer, using the back of a wooden spoon to break up the tomatoes as they cook.
  3. Reduce heat to low and cook uncovered, stirring occasionally, for about 45 minutes, until the fat separates and floats free on the surface.

docs.title: 2. Finish
docs.text:
1. Remove and discard the onion halves.
  2. Taste, then add salt only if needed.

docs.title: 3. Serve
docs.text: Toss with cooked pasta, or use as needed.

docs.title: Easy Pizza Dough
docs.text: easy same-day dough for practicing on super hot ovens

docs.title: Dough
docs.text:
• Bread flour or all-purpose flour: 300 g (≈ 2½ cups)
  • Water, lukewarm: 180 g (≈ ¾ cup)
  • Fine sea salt: 6 g (≈ 1 tsp)
  • Olive oil: 6 g (≈ 1½ tsp)
  • Instant yeast: 2 g (≈ ½ tsp)
  • Sugar (optional, helps browning): 4 g (≈ 1 tsp)

docs.title: 1. Mix
docs.text:
1. Add flour, yeast, salt, and sugar (if using) to a mixing bowl.
  2. Pour in the water and olive oil.
  3. Mix until no dry flour remains; the dough should be shaggy but cohesive.

docs.title: 2. Rest
docs.text:
1. Cover the bowl.
  2. Let the dough rest for 20 minutes to relax the gluten and improve stretchability.

docs.title: 3. Knead and Ferment
docs.text:
1. Knead the dough in the bowl or on the counter for 1–2 minutes, just until smoother.
  2. Cover and let rise at room temperature for 1–1½ hours, until roughly doubled in size.
  3. Divide into 2 dough balls (about 245 g each).
  4. Lightly oil, cover, and rest for 30 minutes.

docs.title: 4. Stretch and Bake
docs.text:
1. Preheat the electric pizza oven on maximum power for at least 20 minutes.
  2. Lightly flour the dough and press from the center outward, leaving a thicker rim.
  3. Stretch to 10–11 inches. Top the pizza.
  4. Dust the peel with semolina or coarse cornmeal and launch the pizza.
  5. Rotate every 15–20 seconds and bake for 2½–4 minutes, until the bottom is set and lightly charred and the rim is well colored.

docs.title: 5. Serve
docs.text:
1. Remove the pizza from the oven.
  2. Rest briefly, slice, and serve hot.

docs.title: No-Knead Pan Pizza
docs.text: Adapted from the No-Knead Pan Pizza recipe on King Arthur Baking.

docs.title: Crust
docs.text:
• 1/2 cup plus 2 tablespoons (142 g) water, lukewarm
  • 1 tablespoon (13 g) olive oil
  • 1 1/2 cups plus 2 tablespoons (202 g) King Arthur Pizza Flour Blend
  • 1 tablespoon King Arthur Pizza Dough Flavor, optional
  • 1 teaspoon instant yeast
  • 3/4 teaspoon table salt

docs.title: Topping
docs.text:
• 8 ounces (227 g) tomatoes in purée, crushed
  • 1 teaspoon King Arthur Pizza Seasoning or dried Italian herbs
  • 1 1/2 cups (170 g) mozzarella cheese, shredded
  • 2 ounces (57 g) pepperoni
  • 1/4 cup (25 g) Parmesan cheese, grated

docs.title: 1. Prepare the Pan & Dough
docs.text:
1. Grease an 11"-diameter deep-dish pizza pan or a 9" × 13" pan.
  2. Stir the crust ingredients together to form a slightly sticky, soft dough.
  3. Cover and let the dough rise for 30 minutes.

docs.title: 2. Shape the Dough
docs.text:
1. Place the dough in the prepared pan and cover; let rest 10–15 minutes.
  2. Press and stretch the dough to cover the bottom of the pan.
  3. Cover and let rest another 30 minutes.

docs.title: 3. Assemble & Bake
docs.text:
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F with a rack in the center.
  2. In a bowl, combine the crushed tomatoes with the pizza seasoning.
  3. Spread the seasoned tomatoes over the crust.
  4. Sprinkle on the mozzarella and pepperoni, then the Parmesan.
  5. Bake for 15–20 minutes, until the topping is bubbly and golden.

docs.title: 4. Serve
docs.text:
1. Remove the pizza from the oven and carefully lift it out of the pan onto a rack.
  2. Let cool about 15 minutes before cutting and serving.

docs.title: Sourdough Discard Pizza Crust
docs.text: Adapted from the King Arthur Baking recipe on kingarthurbaking.com.

docs.title: Dough
docs.text:
• 1 cup (227 g) sourdough starter, unfed/discard
  • 1/2 cup plus 2 tablespoons to 3/4 cup (141 g to 170 g) water, lukewarm
  • 2 1/2 cups (300 g) all-purpose flour
  • 1 teaspoon table salt
  • 1/2 teaspoon instant yeast or active dry yeast
  • 4 teaspoons pizza dough flavor, optional

docs.title: 1. Mix the Dough
docs.text:
1. Stir any liquid on top of your refrigerated starter back into it, then measure 1 cup (227 g) into a large mixing bowl.
  2. Combine the lesser amount of water, all the flour, salt, yeast, and pizza dough flavor with the sourdough starter.
  3. Mix to combine, adding remaining water 1 tablespoon at a time if the dough looks dry.
  4. Knead about 7 minutes (stand mixer with dough hook) until the dough cleans the sides of the bowl.

docs.title: 2. First Rise
docs.text: 1. Place the dough in a lightly greased container, cover, and let rise until nearly doubled, about 2 to 4 hours depending on the vitality of your starter.

docs.title: 3. Shape
docs.text:
1. For two thin-crust pizzas: divide the dough in half and shape each piece into a flattened disk. Drizzle two 12-inch pizza pans with olive oil and brush to coat.
  2. Place the dough in the pans, cover, and let rest 15 minutes. Press the dough toward the edges; if it springs back, let it rest another 15 minutes and continue.
  3. For a thicker crust: oil a 14-inch round pizza pan or an 18 x 13-inch half-sheet pan. Press the dough to the edges, resting 15 minutes if it shrinks back.
  4. Cover the pan and let the dough rise until as thick as you like.

docs.title: 4. Bake
docs.text:
1. Toward the end of the rise, preheat the oven to 450°F.
  2. Add sauce and toppings, leaving the cheese off initially for a crispier crust.
  3. For thin crust: bake 5 minutes, then add cheese and bake about 5 minutes more until the cheese is melted.
  4. For thicker crust: bake 10 minutes, then add cheese and bake about 5 to 7 minutes until the cheese is melted.

docs.title: 5. Serve
docs.text: 1. Remove from the oven and serve hot.

docs.title: Chile Rojo Base
docs.text: Original recipe.

docs.title: Chiles
docs.text:
• 12 dried guajillo chiles
  • 12 dried pasilla chiles

docs.title: Aromatics & Seasoning
docs.text:
• 18 cloves garlic, unpeeled
  • 2 tbsp Mexican oregano
  • 2 tsp Diamond Crystal kosher salt
  • Reserved chile soaking liquid, to consistency

docs.title: 1. Roast Garlic
docs.text: 1. Dry-roast unpeeled garlic cloves in a hot pan 8–10 minutes, turning occasionally, until soft inside. Peel and set aside.

docs.title: 2. Toast and Soak Chiles
docs.text:
1. Stem and seed guajillo and pasilla chiles. Toast in a dry pan, pressing flat, until fragrant and darkening at edges — 2–3 minutes per side.
  2. Transfer to a bowl, cover with hot water, and soak 20–30 minutes. Drain, reserving soaking liquid.

docs.title: 3. Blend
docs.text:
1. Add all ingredients to blender. Blend smooth, adding soaking liquid 1 tbsp at a time until paste is thick and coats a spoon heavily.
  2. Taste and adjust salt.

docs.title: 4. Freeze
docs.text:
1. Pour paste into a gallon freezer bag. Seal, lay flat on a sheet pan, and spread to an even layer approximately 1/4 inch thick.
  2. Score a 2x2 inch grid into the paste using a bench scraper, pressing firmly through the bag to create clean perforations.
  3. Freeze flat. Once frozen, snap portions as needed — one 2x2 square is a standard 2-cube equivalent.

docs.title: Derivatives
docs.text: Dish Adds per 2 cubes base Enchilada sauce Enchilada sauce Chilaquiles Thin with 3/4 cup stock; add splash lime juice Chile colorado Add 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp vinegar; braise meat directly in sauce Arroz rojo 1 cube stirred into rice before adding stock Frijoles 1 cube added to pot after beans are cooked through Tinga Thin with 1/2 cup stock; add 1 chipotle in adobo Adobo/marinade Add 2 tbsp vinegar, 1 tbsp sugar, 2 chipotles in adobo Chilorio sauce Use chilorio sauce recipe

docs.title: Chilorio Sauce
docs.text: Adapted from the Chilorio recipe in La Mesa Mexicana.

docs.title: Chilorio Sauce
docs.text:
• 6 dried guajillo chillies, stemmed and deseeded
  • 1 dried pasilla chilli, stemmed and deseeded
  • ½ teaspoon ground cumin
  • 2 teaspoons ground cinnamon
  • ¼ teaspoon ground cloves
  • 2 bay leaves
  • 1 tablespoon dried oregano
  • 2 garlic cloves, crushed
  • ½ teaspoon Diamond Crystal kosher salt
  • 4 teaspoons white vinegar

docs.title: 1. Rehydrate the Chillies
docs.text: 1. Put the chillies in a small saucepan with 4 cups water and boil for 10 minutes, or until they are soft.

docs.title: 2. Blend the Sauce
docs.text:
1. Put the chillies in a blender with 1 cup of their cooking water.
  2. Add the remaining sauce ingredients and blend to a smooth consistency.

docs.title: 3. Combine with Pork
docs.text: 1. Strain the sauce over the pulled pork and stir over low heat for 3–5 minutes, until warmed through.

docs.title: 4. Serve
docs.text: 1. Serve as tacos with warm tortillas, or use as a filling.

docs.title: Chile Rojo Enchilada Sauce (Roux-Thickened, Small Batch)
docs.text: Adapted from the Enchilada Sauce derivative in the Chile Rojo Base recipe on Jeremy's Recipe Collection.

docs.title: Base & Liquid
docs.text:
• 4 cubes (2 squares) Chile Rojo Base — about 2 tbsp / 32g
  • 1 cup (237 mL) chicken stock

docs.title: Roux & Enrichment
docs.text:
• 1.5 tbsp (21g) lard
  • 1.5 tbsp (12g) all-purpose flour
  • 1 tbsp (16g) tomato paste
  • 1/2 tsp (1g) ground cumin
  • Kosher salt, to taste

docs.title: 1. Make the Roux
docs.text: Melt the lard in a small saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in the flour and cook, whisking constantly, 2-3 minutes, until pale gold and toasty-smelling.

docs.title: 2. Bloom the Paste and Tomato
docs.text: Whisk in the Chile Rojo Base and tomato paste. Cook, stirring, 1-2 minutes until darkened and deeply toasted-smelling.

docs.title: 3. Add Cumin
docs.text: Stir in the cumin and toast 30 seconds.

docs.title: 4. Whisk in Stock
docs.text: Add the stock a splash at a time, whisking out

docs.title: Base
docs.text:
• 2% plain Greek yogurt (Fage 2%) — 180g / ¾ cup
  • Garlic, fresh — 2–3 cloves (about 7g), microplaned
  • Fresh lemon juice — 22ml / 1½ tbsp
  • Extra-virgin olive oil — 10g / ¾ tsp
  • Diamond Crystal kosher salt — 4g / ¾ tsp
  • Water — 30–45ml / 2–3 tbsp

docs.title: 1. Combine
docs.text: Combine ingredients in a bowl and thin with a couple tablespoons water.

docs.title: 2. Bottle

docs.title: Salsa Roja
docs.text:
Adapted from the Salsa Roja recipe in La Mesa Mexicana.

Makes about 1 cup. Enough for 10 tacos.

docs.title: Salsa
docs.text:
• 4 large hothouse (beefsteak) tomatoes, halved
  • ½ white onion, cut into wedges
  • 6 dried arbol chillies
  • ½ garlic clove, skin on
  • 2 teaspoons Diamond Crystal kosher salt
  • 3 tablespoons vegetable oil
  • Fresh coriander (cilantro) leaves, to serve

docs.title: 1. Char
docs.text: Set oven to high broil. Place tomatoes cut side up, onion wedges, and garlic clove (skin on) on a baking sheet. Broil for 10–15 minutes until blackened in spots, adding the garlic in the last few minutes to prevent burning. Peel the garlic before blending.

docs.title: 2. Rehydrate Chillies
docs.text: Place the dried chillies in a small saucepan. Cover with 1 cup water and bring to the boil. Cook for 5–8 minutes, until the chillies are soft. Set aside to cool for 5 minutes, then remove the stems.

docs.title: 3. Blend
docs.text: Using a blender or molcajete, blend or pound the charred tomato and onion with the peeled garlic, salt, chillies and 1 teaspoon of their cooking water, until you have a chunky salsa.

docs.title: Sous Vide Chile-Smoked Pulled Pork (Country-Style Ribs)
docs.text: A personal sous vide workflow.

docs.title: Pork
docs.text: • Boneless country-style pork ribs (Costco), cut into 2–3 inch chunks: ~900 g / 2 lb

docs.title: Dried Chile Powder (makes ~1-1½ Tbsp)
docs.text:
• Dried ancho chiles: 1 whole
  • Dried guajillo chiles: 1 whole
  • Dried árbol chile (optional, for heat): ½ whole

docs.title: Seasoning & Aromatics
docs.text:
• Kosher salt (Diamond Crystal): 10–12 g / ~2 tsp (1–1.25% by weight)
  • Frozen minced garlic: 6–8 g / 1–1½ tsp
  • Chile powder (from above): 4–6 g / 1–1½ tsp
  • Liquid smoke: 1–2 g / ¼–½ tsp
  • Neutral oil or rendered pork fat (optional): 10 g / 2 tsp

docs.title: 1. Make the Chile Powder
docs.text:
1. Remove stems from dried chiles and shake out loose seeds.
  2. Toast chiles in a dry skillet over medium heat, pressing gently, until pliable and fragrant (10–20 seconds per side). Do not scorch.
  3. Cool completely.
  4. Tear into pieces and grind to a fine powder in a spice grinder.
  5. Measure out 1–1½ tsp for the recipe; reserve extra for future use.

docs.title: 2. Season & Bag
docs.text:
1. Cut pork into 2–3 inch chunks for even cooking and increased surface area.
  2. Toss pork with salt, chile powder, garlic, liquid smoke, and optional oil until evenly coated.
  3. Vacuum seal in a single layer if possible.

docs.title: 3. Freeze (Optional)
docs.text:
1. Freeze immediately if not cooking right away.
  2. Pork can go straight from freezer to water bath when ready.

docs.title: 4. Sous Vide
docs.text:
1. Preheat water bath to 154°F / 68°C.
  2. Cook pork for 26–28 hours.
  3. Ensure bag remains fully submerged.

docs.title: 5. Pull & Separate
docs.text:
1. Remove pork from bag while hot.
  2. Pour bag liquid into a gravy separator.
  3. Pull pork into strands using forks or hands; keep warm.

docs.title: 6. Reduce & Recombine
docs.text:
1. Let fat separate fully, then remove and reserve it.
  2. Reduce the defatted liquid gently until lightly syrupy (about 50–65% reduction).
  3. Whisk in ¼–⅓ of the reserved fat until glossy.
  4. Gradually toss sauce into pulled pork until moist and lightly coated.

docs.title: 7. Serve or Store
docs.text:
1. If serving immediately, use pork as-is for tacos, burritos, or rice bowls. Can crisp up portions in a foil-lined sheet pan under the broiler or on the stove in a skillet.
  2. For later use, transfer pulled pork and sauce to airtight containers.
  3. Let cool uncovered for 15–20 minutes, then seal and refrigerate.

docs.title: Steak
docs.text:
• Ribeye steaks, ~1 inch thick (as many as needed)
  • Diamond Crystal kosher salt

docs.title: Sear
docs.text: • Avocado or grapeseed oil — ~1 tsp (5ml) per batch

docs.title: Optional Browned Butter Finish
docs.text:
• Unsalted butter — ~2 tbsp per steak
  • 1–2 garlic cloves, smashed
  • Fresh rosemary
  • Flaky finishing salt

docs.title: 1. Dry Brine
docs.text: Season steaks generously with Diamond Crystal kosher salt on all sides. Place uncovered on a rack in the fridge for a minimum of 2 hours, ideally overnight.

docs.title: 2. Sous Vide
docs.text: Bag steaks and cook at 133°F using the Breville Joule guide for time based on thickness. For ~1 inch ribeyes this is typically 1–1.5 hours.

docs.title: 3. Dry the Surface
docs.text: Remove steaks from bags and pat thoroughly dry with paper towels for a full 5 minutes. Take your time here — a dry surface is essential for crust development.

docs.title: 4. Preheat the Pan
docs.text: Set carbon steel over medium-high heat until just starting to smoke. IR gun should read around 300–320°F. Add a thin film of high smoke point oil — pan will jump to ~500°F immediately. Open windows, put hood to high.

docs.title: 5. Sear
docs.text: Sear steaks 3 minutes total, flipping every 30 seconds. Hit the edges against the pan wall for 15–20 seconds per side.

docs.title: 6. Browned Butter Finish (optional)
docs.text: In a small saucepan over medium heat, melt butter with smashed garlic and thyme or rosemary if using. Cook until milk solids are golden and nutty, 3–4 minutes. Pour over rested steaks.

docs.title: 7. Serve
docs.text: Rest 5 minutes, slice against the grain, finish with flaky salt, and enjoy.

  • Neutral oil (enough to coat)
  • Diamond Crystal kosher salt
  • Black pepper

docs.title: 1. Preheat the Pan
docs.text: Place a sheet pan in the oven and preheat to 500°F. Allow the pan to heat fully before cooking.

docs.title: 2. Prep the Broccoli
docs.text: Break the broccoli down into florets. Toss with oil and season well with salt and pepper.

docs.title: 3. Roast
docs.text: Carefully transfer the seasoned florets to the hot sheet pan in a single layer. Roast for approximately 12 minutes, until deeply browned and caramelized at the edges.

docs.title: 4. Serve

docs.title: Roasted Cabbage
docs.text: Adapted from the America’s Test Kitchen recipe.

docs.title: Cabbage
docs.text:
• 1 head green cabbage (2 to 2½ pounds)
  • 3 tablespoons vegetable oil, divided
  • 1 teaspoon kosher salt, divided
  • ¼ teaspoon pepper

docs.title: 1. Prep the Cabbage
docs.text:
1. Adjust oven rack to upper-middle position and heat oven to 500°F.
  2. Quarter cabbage through core and cut each quarter into 2 wedges, leaving core intact.
  3. Arrange wedges, 1 flat side down, on rimmed baking sheet.

docs.title: 2. Season and Steam-Roast
docs.text:
1. Brush 1½ tablespoons oil on exposed cut sides of wedges and sprinkle with ½ teaspoon salt.
  2. Flip wedges so oiled sides are flush with sheet.
  3. Brush second cut sides with remaining 1½ tablespoons oil and sprinkle with pepper and remaining ½ teaspoon salt.
  4. Cover sheet tightly with aluminum foil and roast for 20 minutes.

docs.title: 3. Uncover and Brown
docs.text:
1. Remove foil (be careful of escaping steam) and continue to cook until cabbage wedges begin to brown on underside, 5 to 10 minutes.
  2. Using tongs and thin metal spatula, flip each wedge.
  3. Roast until edges are very well browned and some leaves have crisped, 5 to 10 minutes.

docs.title: 4. Serve
docs.text: 1. Transfer to serving platter, season with salt and pepper to taste, and serve.
